Produce.note: v8 per-record errors (KIP-467), v9 flexible, v10 leader hints (KIP-951), v11 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890), v12 transaction-version-2 implicit add-partitions (KIP-890 part 2), v13 topic IDs (KIP-516, Kafka 4.1; may return UNKNOWN_TOPIC_ID).

Fetch.note: v11 rack / preferred read replica (KIP-392): the wire fields exist but the follower out-of-range and OFFSET_NOT_AVAILABLE handling does not. v12 flexible + LastFetchedEpoch, v13 topic IDs replace names (KIP-516), v14 OFFSET_MOVED_TO_TIERED_STORAGE (KIP-405), v15 ReplicaState (KIP-903), v16 leader hints (KIP-951), v17 ReplicaDirectoryId (KIP-853), v18 HighWatermark (KIP-1166).

ListOffsets.note: v4 leader epoch (KIP-320), v6 flexible, v7 max-timestamp (KIP-734), v8 earliest-local offset (KIP-405), v9 last-tiered offset (KIP-1005). v10 (async remote list offsets, KIP-1075) and v11 (earliest pending upload offset, KIP-1023) are deliberate gaps, not a waiver: both are tiered-storage features this client does not use.

Metadata.note: v7 leader epoch (KIP-320), v9 flexible, v10+ topic IDs, v13 adds a top-level error code and is where REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED surfaces (KIP-1102).

OffsetCommit.note: v6 committed leader epoch (KIP-320), v7 group instance id, v8 flexible, v9 member epoch (KIP-848), v10 topic IDs.

OffsetFetch.note: v5 leader epoch, v6 flexible, v7 require-stable (KIP-447), v8 multi-group batching, v9 member epoch (KIP-848), v10 topic IDs. The fork has no v0 codec, which is correct: v0 read offsets from ZooKeeper.

FindCoordinator.note: v3 flexible, v4 multi-key batch (KIP-699), v5 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890), v6 KeyType SHARE=2 (KIP-932, broker-internal). apiKeys.js still calls key 10 GroupCoordinator, the pre-0.11 name.

JoinGroup.note: v5 encodes groupInstanceId but nothing plumbs it: Broker.joinGroup() has no such parameter, so static membership (KIP-345) is inert today.

LeaveGroup.note: v3 batch removal by group instance id (KIP-345): the codec exists, but there is no admin removeMembersFromConsumerGroup to drive it.

DescribeGroups.note: Below v6 the broker reports KIP-848 consumer-protocol groups as Dead; v6 adds ErrorMessage. Full coverage also needs ConsumerGroupDescribe (key 69) routing.

ListGroups.note: No GroupState filter (v4) or GroupType field (v5), so consumer-protocol groups cannot be told apart from classic ones.

SaslHandshake.note: Never flexible, and the only API in the matrix that is fully current.

ApiVersions.note: v0-v3 omit every SupportedFeatures entry whose MinVersion is 0 (KAFKA-17011, fixed in v4 / Kafka 3.9), so a v3-only client sees a truncated feature list. The flexible-protocol pilot targets v4 and falls back to v3 only for brokers below 3.9.

CreateTopics.note: v5 flexible, v7 returns topic IDs.

DeleteTopics.note: v6 deletes by topic ID. The fork's v1 sits exactly on the 4.x floor.

InitProducerId.note: v2+ is flexible, so even v3 needs the flexible-protocol work first. v3 producer-id/epoch re-init (KIP-360), v4 PRODUCER_FENCED, v5 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE, v6 two-phase commit (KIP-939) and latestVersionUnstable, so brokers advertise 0-5 by default.

AddPartitionsToTxn.note: Unused under transaction version 2 (KIP-890 part 2), where Produce carries the add-partitions call.

EndTxn.note: v5 returns a bumped producer id and epoch under transaction version 2. The TV2 signal is the transaction.version finalized feature in ApiVersions v3+, not EndTxn's advertised max version.

TxnOffsetCommit.note: v2 adds the committed leader epoch; v3 is KIP-447 group metadata, which the fork does not implement at all.

DescribeAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

CreateAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

DeleteAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

AlterConfigs.note: IncrementalAlterConfigs (key 44) is the modern replacement and is unimplemented, so config changes still overwrite rather than merge.

AlterPartitionReassignments.note: One of the only two flexible-encoded codecs in the fork today: it hand-rolls the tag buffer inside the request body because the request header is still hardcoded to v1. It must migrate when real flexible header selection lands. v1 adds AllowReplicationFactorChange.

ListPartitionReassignments.note: The other hand-rolled flexible codec; same migration applies. Kafka defines only v0, so the fork is current by accident.

OffsetForLeaderEpoch.note: Leader-epoch fencing (KIP-320). Without it an unclean leader change can silently duplicate or skip records.

IncrementalAlterConfigs.note: The replacement for AlterConfigs; needed before any admin config change can be merge-semantics rather than overwrite.

ConsumerGroupHeartbeat.note: Required for the KIP-848 consumer group protocol (groupProtocol: 'consumer'), GA since Kafka 4.0.

ConsumerGroupDescribe.note: Admin-side counterpart of KIP-848; needed so group descriptions stop reporting consumer-protocol groups as Dead.

DescribeTopicPartitions.note: Admin describe at scale, and the only way to read eligible leader replicas. The API does not exist on brokers below 3.8, so the Metadata path must stay as a fallback; ELR arrays are null unless the cluster runs eligible.leader.replicas.version=1.

crossCutting.gap: Version negotiation ignores the broker's advertised minimum version
crossCutting.impact: Under a raised KIP-896 floor the client silently sends a version the broker rejects instead of failing with a clear error. This is what makes the below-floor list below dangerous rather than merely dead.

crossCutting.gap: No topic-ID (UUID) awareness anywhere in cluster metadata
crossCutting.where: cluster metadata, fetch and offset paths
crossCutting.impact: Blocks Fetch v13+, Produce v13, OffsetCommit/OffsetFetch v10, DeleteTopics v6, CreateTopics v7 ids, KIP-848 assignments, and exact topic-recreation detection.
Every poll sends a full fetch request; incremental fetch is a prerequisite for efficient modern Fetch versions.

crossCutting.gap: Compression codecs: no built-in zstd (KIP-110) and no bundled LZ4
crossCutting.impact: Users must register LZ4 themselves; zstd-compressed batches cannot be read or written out of the box.
Recovery after every known broker rotates away is accidental rather than designed: no metadata reset, no metadata.recovery.* options, no REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED (code 129) handling.
Unreachable against a 4.x broker, which never negotiates Produce below v3 or Fetch below v4. The decoders must stay: old segments can still be returned inside a modern Fetch response.

UNKNOWN.reason: KafkaJS has exposed this name as KafkaJSProtocolError.type since 1.x; renaming it is a breaking public-API change.

NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 2.6 (KIP-392); the KafkaJS name is public API.

GROUP_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11 when coordinators stopped being group-only; the KafkaJS name is public API.

GROUP_COORDINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11; the KafkaJS name is public API.

NOT_COORDINATOR_FOR_GROUP.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11; the KafkaJS name is public API.
